title: Global Oil Prices Tumble Again

image.attribution: Mario Roberto Duran Ortiz / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-3.0

main_content:
World oil prices tumbled again, dropping to lows not seen since late 2008 and early 2009, when the global recession was deepening.

Global crude prices have been falling for months, with the latest plunge coming as Iran renewed its pledge to boost its crude exports, adding to the glut of oil on the world market.

Oil produced in the United States fell below $35 a barrel in early trading, although the price recovered somewhat in the hours afterward to reach $35.27.

Even with declining world prices, Iran’s deputy oil minister, Amir Hossein Zamaninia, said there was “absolutely no chance” that Tehran would delay its plan to increase its oil exports. The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, whose 13 member nations produce about 35 percent of the world oil supply, has effectively abandoned oil production quotas, adding to the world oil glut.

The International Energy Agency says it expects the oil glut will extend to at least late 2016, with OPEC showing “renewed determination” to maximize its production.

The cut in the price of crude on the world market has led to the lowest gasoline prices in several years for motorists in the United States. But the steady drop in prices has hindered economies in oil-producing countries dependent on oil revenues, such as Venezuela and Russia. Energy companies have had to scramble to pay bills and fund new operations and sometimes have laid off workers.

questions.question: When have oil prices last been so low?
options: During the global financial crisis of 2008-2009
At the start of the COVID-19 pandemic
questions.answer: During the global financial crisis of 2008-2009

questions.question: Why have oil prices plunged again?
options: Due to increased demand from emerging markets
Because of Iran’s commitment to raise its crude exports
As a result of OPEC enforcing stricter production quotas
Following natural disasters affecting oil production
questions.answer: Because of Iran’s commitment to raise its crude exports

questions.question: How did Iran react to the current oil price?
options: By agreeing to cut its production to stabilize prices
With plans to maintain and increase its oil exports
By suspending all oil exports until prices improve
By expressing concerns over economic impacts on its budget
questions.answer: With plans to maintain and increase its oil exports
